gaps.lead: If Marc hadn't taken up politics, he might have become a famous art historian.
gaps.sentence: If Marc hadn't taken up politics, he might have ___ himself as an art historian.
gaps.hint: become famous = make a ___ for oneself
gaps.explanation: 'Make a name for himself' means become well known.

gaps.lead: He would rather not talk about the accident.
Pay claims must be submitted before the end of the month.
gaps.sentence: You have ___ your pay claims before the end of the month.
gaps.explanation: 'Must be submitted' becomes 'you have to put in your claims'.

gaps.lead: A mechanic repaired my father's roof last week.
gaps.explanation: have something done = arrange for somebody to do it: had his roof repaired.

gaps.lead: 'I will definitely complete the report by Friday,' I said.
gaps.explanation: commit oneself TO + -ing: committed myself to finishing.

gaps.lead: They have accused the mayor of corruption.
gaps.explanation: Active 'they have accused him of' becomes passive: has been accused of.
